compiled_state.title: Story 20d7 deleted per-branch-review.yml — unrelated functionality removed for epic invariant convenience (scope regression pattern)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

Story 20d7-09d6-b831-4c3a (under epic b575) deleted .github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml (commit 4b18d2d644, task 398c-9d6c-1fd5-4b39) to satisfy an epic-internal invariant ('exactly one llm-review pipeline per SHA' needed by cycle-ledger story 5621, arbiter dispatch story b1b6, max_cycles enforcement story 35b8).

The deleted workflow provided the project's per-story / per-batch internal LLM review surface — the SUB-PR review tier that the user has repeatedly identified as load-bearing for reliable review of large epics.

## Scope violation pattern

The epic's stated goal (b575) is cycle-end arbiter + workflow unification. It was NOT scoped to remove existing review coverage. Deleting per-branch-review.yml is a regression introduced because the new functionality interfered with the old, not because the old functionality was wrong.

The right architectural choice was to KEY THE LEDGER BY (PR, SHA) instead of SHA alone, so parallel review workflows could coexist without double-counting. Story 20d7 took the destructive path instead.

## Compounding misclosure

Story 20d7's completion-verifier caught the gap and filed bug 0091-0cf9-3840-4b00. Bug 0091 was CLOSED via commit 4c730cf6db that only edited debug-everything/SKILL.md to point at /dso:review — a skill that is HARD-GATED to no-op under dso.workflow=ci-pr. The 'fix' was documentation-only and pointed at a code path that does not run in production mode.

Tracking history:
- Original ticket: b1a7-20bf-88a1-4fb5 (closed; this is the recreation without parent)
- Original deletion task: 398c-9d6c-1fd5-4b39
- Original story: 20d7-09d6-b831-4c3a
- Misclosed gap bug: 0091-0cf9-3840-4b00

## Why this is P0

- User has repeatedly stated that every change must pass review before merging to main
- This is the SECOND critical workflow regression in this epic
- Pattern: stories that interfere with existing functionality delete the existing functionality instead of reconciling

## Resolution path

Coverage restoration is in scope of the upcoming remediation epic (will explicitly include SC to restore per-sub-PR review with no-duplicate-checks invariant via ledger keying).

This bug remains as the POST-MORTEM RECORD documenting the scope-regression pattern for future process work AFTER the remediation epic stabilizes the workflow. The bug captures the systemic issue (stories delete unrelated functionality when convenient); the remediation epic only addresses the symptom. Dedicated focused work post-remediation should investigate enforcement mechanisms that prevent this pattern (story-planning gate, scope-classification rubric, etc.) — CLAUDE.md additions are NOT effective per user direction.

comments.body:
BASIC investigation complete (agent afd0). 5 hypothesis tests run; 4 confirmed + 1 disproved. Empirical findings:
- per-branch-review.yml absent on HEAD (ls -la exits 1).
- Commit 4b18d2d644 (story 20d7, task 398c) deleted 310 lines: '.github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml | 310 --------------------------------'. Commit subject: 'fix(workflow): delete per-branch-review.yml to enforce single llm-review per SHA (GREEN)'. Confirmed.
- Commit 4c730cf6db (bug 0091 'fix') is documentation-only: only debug-everything/SKILL.md + sprint/SKILL.md modified (11+/12-); no code change. Both SKILL.md files now contain 'KNOWN GAP' blocks explicitly stating '/dso:review is HARD-GATED to no-op under dso.workflow=ci-pr' and 'per-sub-branch internal LLM review is currently NOT firing.' Confirmed.
- dso.workflow=ci-pr active in .claude/dso-config.conf — meaning /dso:review would indeed no-op in production. Confirmed.
- No remediation epic exists: scanned 143 open epics for per-branch/sub-pr/ledger/review-coverage/llm-review-pipeline keywords. The 5 'remediation' epics found (2687, 5efb, 83e2, c821, w21) are unrelated to review-pipeline restoration. Disproved (the ticket's 'upcoming remediation epic' has not been created).

Fix complexity: COMPLEX — multi-subsystem cross-cutting work spanning (a) restore per-branch-review.yml with scoped sub-branch PR trigger + dedup vs ci.yml llm-review, (b) refactor cycle-ledger keying from SHA to (PR, SHA), (c) add story-planning governance gate that blocks destructive deletions of review-surface workflows as an acceptable resolution to 'duplicate check' invariants, (d) sequence (a)-(c) via a dedicated remediation epic with preplanning. Per CLAUDE.md rule:bug-close-with-code (no code fix possible) AND per the ticket's own stated resolution path ('upcoming remediation epic … POST-MORTEM RECORD'), this bug remains OPEN. Not autonomously invoking /dso:brainstorm — epic creation requires explicit user direction per the ticket text.

comments.body:
EVIDENCE (2026-05-23): sprint of epic 81d7-9da2-676e-4948 just merged 3 story-to-session PRs that confirm and extend the symptom:

PR #292 (story a7c0-8e53 → session worktree-20260522-180209): llm-review status = SKIPPED (gated to base_ref == 'main')
PR #293 (story ab28-87ea → session worktree-20260522-180209): llm-review status = SKIPPED + Lint Python (ruff) FAILED with auto-merge race (actions/checkout couldn't fetch refs/remotes/pull/293/merge because PR had already been auto-merged)
PR #294 (story b2b0-40b9 → session worktree-20260522-180209): llm-review status = SKIPPED + Script Tests FAILED with orphan-process kill (job terminated mid-run by auto-merge)

EXTENDED FINDING beyond the original 576b symptom: branch protection on the session branch does not require Lint Python or Script Tests as a passing condition for merge. Auto-merge fires when the *required* subset (Ticket tests, ShellCheck, Hook Tests, Portability Smoke) is green, before slower checks finish. So even the *remaining* CI checks (after llm-review skip) do not all run to completion before squash-merge. This means story→session PRs merge with even less coverage than the SKILL.md documented gap implies.

The user has now flagged the missing llm-review on these PRs. As a compensating control for this sprint run, a local code review will be executed on each PR's diff. The systemic resolution remains the remediation epic referenced in the original ticket body.
